title: Cannot properly use Web builds with Address/Leak Sanitizer enabled (despite claimed as supported in the docs)
body:
### Tested versions

Tested when building web export templates on Godot 4.5.1.

### System information

Windows 10, Godot v4.5.1-stable

### Issue description

I'm trying to debug a bizzare crash that I'm facing on iPhone Safari Web builds launched inside Youtube Playables.
I'm testing on an iPhone 12 (but seems to crash on modern models as well) using Godot 4.5.1.

For context: the game seems to crash without much symptoms: first it starts to stutter after some time, then crashes. Even an empty-ish project crashes (rotating sprite and some Control nodes, minimal load).
The crash happens regardless of user tapping the screen (stutters start around 40 mins in an idle project, crashes around 60-90 minutes in). Tapping the screen somehow accelerates the proccess (stutters at 10-15 mins in, crash at 15-20).

I've exhausted most other ways of finding the problem and wanted to detect a memory leak using Sanitizers (and I'm pretty sure it's a memory leak of some sort, as Safari tab receives a memory pressure warning fromthe iOS system, but Godot Debug Monitors do not report anything wrong).

Does anyone know how to properly trigger logging from sanitizers (e.g. from `use_asan=true`/`use_lsan=true` compile flags) in a web build?
I've tried `get_tree.quit(`) but that doesn't seem to do anything... the app just freezes. Same happens trying to call `__lsan_do_leak_check()`/`__lsan_do_recoverable_leak_check()` manually.

In the browser console (trying to test it first on PC using Firefox/Chrome) I sometimes get errors like:
```
Uncaught (in promise) CompileError: wasm validation error: at offset 372032649: failed to start custom section
    instantiateWasm https://localhost:8060/index.js:12794
    Godot https://localhost:8060/index.js:606
    createWasm https://localhost:8060/index.js:605
    Godot https://localhost:8060/index.js:12131
    Engine https://localhost:8060/index.js:12970
    promise callback*SafeEngine/init/doInit/Engine< https://localhost:8060/index.js:12968
    doInit https://localhost:8060/index.js:12967
    init https://localhost:8060/index.js:12984
    startGame https://localhost:8060/index.js:13079
    <anonymous> https://localhost:8060/:311
    <anonymous> https://localhost:8060/:325
```
When building with asan/lsan. Sometimes it's `wasm validation error: at offset unused values not explicitly dropped by end of block...`

Having some sort of example project/guide for properly making sanitizers work on the Web would be really appreciated.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Build a custom web export template with `use_asan=true` or `use_lsan=true` .
2. Launch it on a server.
3. Load from a PC browser, open the console.
4. Trigger the leak information by calling `get_tree.quit(`) from GDScipt or `__lsan_do_leak_check()`/`__lsan_do_recoverable_leak_check()` from C++.
5. Notice a freeze that doesn't resolve itself.
6. Some web build configurations fail to load (possibly due to WASM size?) and show errors (mentioned above).

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

Seems somewhat irrelevant? An empty project works fine, but web export templates need to be compiled manually.
